title: Align ToolSearch tool with the TS baseline
objective: Implement all ToolSearch improvements identified by the per-tool subagent report so the Go clone matches the original TypeScript tool in public contract, runtime logic, robustness, state lifecycle, and tests.

context.problem: Go ToolSearch has a working deferred-tool discovery loop, structured ToolReferenceBlock results, registry visibility filtering, dynamic MCP tool support, cache/index helpers, and several local tests. It is still not fully aligned with the TypeScript reference. The most important differences are that Go exposes a different input schema (`limit` instead of TS `max_results`), routes keyword searches through BM25/embedding behavior instead of the TS fixed keyword scorer and fast paths, lacks TS's per-request enablement gates and provider-specific defer_loading/beta handling, does not announce deferred-tool deltas during normal turns, and does not reliably preserve loaded deferred tools across compaction/resume. Some existing Go alignment tests encode non-TS expectations, so they currently protect divergences rather than parity.

parallelization_notes: Can be assigned to an implementation subagent after listed dependencies are available. Avoid running concurrently with another task that owns the same files.

improvement_points.title: Go exposes `limit` while TS exposes `max_results`
improvement_points.description: The TS input schema is `{ query: string, max_results?: number }` with a default of 5. Go's public schema advertises `limit`, min/max bounds, and no `max_results`; it only accepts `max_results` as a hidden legacy struct field. This changes the model-facing API and can make TS-compatible callers invisible to schema-driven prompting while making Go-generated `limit` calls invalid against the TS tool.

improvement_points.title: Go Execute uses BM25/embedding ranking instead of TS keyword scorer and fast paths
improvement_points.description: TS keyword search has explicit behavior: bare exact tool name returns directly, `mcp__server` prefix returns prefix matches directly, `+term` filters candidates by name/description/searchHint, and scores with fixed weights over parsed name parts, searchHint, and prompt description. Go's Execute path builds a ToolIndex and BM25Ranker, optionally reranks embeddings, and never calls the preserved TS-like `searchToolsWithKeywords` helper. This loses TS fast paths; for example a bare CamelCase tool name can tokenize differently from the indexed expanded identifier.

improvement_points.title: Go result shape and model-facing prompt differ from TS
improvement_points.description: TS declares a typed output object with `matches`, `query`, `total_deferred_tools`, and optional `pending_mcp_servers`, then maps successful results to pure `tool_reference` content blocks. Go returns a ToolResult with prose summaries, optional metadata (`scores`, `rerank`, MCP state strings), and ToolReferenceBlocks; its prompt describes BM25 scores/snippets rather than the TS deferred-tool-location and result-format contract. On empty results, TS emits the fixed text `No matching deferred tools found` plus a pending-server sentence only when applicable; Go includes query text, deferred pool count, missing names, and richer MCP-state prose/metadata.

improvement_points.title: ToolSearch enablement is static in Go instead of TS per-request gating
improvement_points.description: TS has an optimistic base-tool inclusion check, then a definitive per-request `isToolSearchEnabled` check that considers environment mode, experimental beta kill switch, provider/proxy support, model support, ToolSearch availability after permissions/disallowed filtering, and auto-threshold sizing. It also disables ToolSearch for a request when there are no deferred tools and no pending MCP servers. Go registers ToolSearch once during SetupRegistry from a simplified env check and Registry.VisibleTools hides deferred tools whenever ToolSearch is registered, with no model, provider, permission/disallowed, auto-threshold, or no-deferred/pending request gate.

improvement_points.title: Provider `defer_loading`, beta headers, and stale tool_reference stripping are not TS-equivalent
improvement_points.description: TS adds provider-specific tool-search beta headers only when request-time ToolSearch is enabled, marks deferred tool schemas with `defer_loading`, and strips tool_reference blocks when tool search is disabled or a referenced tool is no longer available. Go ToolDefinition has no `defer_loading` field, Anthropic beta header logic is hard-coded to the 1P header from env rather than the request's provider/model gate, and Anthropic conversion serializes ToolReferenceBlocks unconditionally whenever they exist.

improvement_points.title: Go lacks TS per-turn deferred-tools delta announcements
improvement_points.description: TS announces deferred tools during normal attachment generation via `deferred_tools_delta` system reminders, or falls back to prepending an `<available-deferred-tools>` message when the delta gate is off. Go only has a post-compaction deferred-tools reminder; there is no normal-turn ToolSearch attachment in providerParams or loop attachment injection. That means the model may not see the TS-equivalent list of deferred tool names before it decides whether to use `select:<name>`.

improvement_points.title: Loaded deferred tools are not reliably preserved across compaction and resume
improvement_points.description: TS reconstructs discovered tools by scanning nested tool_reference blocks inside tool_result content and by reading `preCompactDiscoveredTools` from compact boundary metadata. Go's live loop learns nested ToolReferenceBlocks from tool results during the current run, but compaction metadata extraction scans only top-level message blocks, so it misses the actual nested ToolSearch result shape. Repository search also shows no QueryLoop constructor/resume path that rebuilds `loadedToolNames` from existing messages or compact boundary metadata.

improvement_points.title: MCP pending-state and list_changed invalidation hooks exist but are not wired like TS runtime state
improvement_points.description: TS ToolSearch consults appState MCP clients on every empty result and reports pending server names. Go has global resolver hooks for pending/full MCP visibility state, and dynamic-MCP list_changed invalidator helpers, but repository search shows the resolver setters are only used by tests and SetupRegistry does not install list_changed invalidators for the production ToolSearch instance. As a result, empty ToolSearch misses normally omit TS pending_mcp_servers information, and dynamic MCP changes can rely on manual/test wiring rather than runtime wiring.

improvement_points.title: Go lacks TS tool_reference message-normalization safeguards
improvement_points.description: TS has dedicated normalization for tool_reference blocks: strip all references when ToolSearch is disabled, strip references for unavailable tools, avoid mixing tool_reference with text inside a tool_result, and inject/relocate sibling text to avoid provider/model stop-sequence pathologies. Go serializes structured tool results directly to provider-specific formats and does not implement equivalent normalization before Anthropic/OpenAI/Responses conversion.

improvement_points.title: Current Go ToolSearch alignment tests assert non-TS behavior
improvement_points.description: Several Go tests labeled as TS alignment encode `limit`, min/max clamping, BM25 ranking, score metadata, snippets, and embedding rerank metadata as desired parity. The TS files provided as the benchmark show `max_results`, fixed keyword scoring, and no scores/snippets/rerank fields in the output schema. This gives a false positive on parity and leaves the actual TS behaviors unprotected.

improvement_points.title: Analytics, read-only metadata, and result-size controls are not aligned with TS
improvement_points.description: TS ToolSearch logs `tengu_tool_search_outcome` with query, queryType, matchCount, totalDeferredTools, maxResults, and hasMatches; declares itself read-only; and sets maxResultSizeChars to 100000. Go has a ToolSearchOutcomeFn hook but the event omits query/maxResults and is not wired outside tests. Go ToolSearch implements IsConcurrentSafe but no IsReadOnly marker and no ToolSearch-specific maxResultSizeChars metadata/threshold.

implementation_subtasks.title: Restore the TS ToolSearch input schema
acceptance_criteria: ToolSearch Schema().Properties contains `query` and `max_results` and does not advertise `limit` as the canonical parameter.
`max_results` defaults to 5 when absent, matching TS.
Existing hidden compatibility for `limit` is either removed or explicitly kept behind tests that prove it is not model-facing.
Tests no longer claim TS uses `limit` or [1,50] clamping.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Change the model-facing schema from `limit` to TS `max_results`, remove TS-incompatible min/max schema claims unless a true TS bound is added upstream, and make Execute semantics match TS defaulting without advertising Go-only fields.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align Execute search semantics with TS keyword search
acceptance_criteria: Bare exact deferred and already-loaded tool names return that tool without ranking.
`mcp__server` prefix queries return matching deferred MCP tools before generic keyword scoring.
`+term` required filters use TS name/description/searchHint logic.
Ranking fixtures match TS fixed-weight ordering, including tie behavior where applicable.
Embedding rerank and BM25-specific score/snippet output do not affect ToolSearch parity mode.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Make the production Execute path follow the TS searchToolsWithKeywords algorithm: bare exact names, MCP prefix fast path, `select:` multi-select, `+` required terms, fixed scoring weights, and max_results slicing. BM25/cache/embedding helpers can remain only if they do not alter the TS-visible behavior, or should be moved behind non-parity experiments outside ToolSearch.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align ToolSearch output and prompt contract
acceptance_criteria: ToolSearch description no longer advertises BM25 scores/snippets as the contract.
Successful Anthropic tool_result content is a list of tool_reference blocks without Go-only score/snippet text mixed into the same structured result.
Empty result text matches TS wording and appends the TS pending-server sentence only when pending_mcp_servers are present.
If Go retains ToolResult metadata for internal observability, provider-bound output remains TS-compatible.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Make the Go tool's model-facing description and result mapping match TS: TS query forms, deferred-tool location hint, typed matches/query/total_deferred_tools/pending_mcp_servers data where the Go tool-result abstraction can carry it, success mapped to tool_reference content blocks, and empty-result text compatible with TS.

implementation_subtasks.title: Implement request-time ToolSearch enablement and visibility gates
acceptance_criteria: ToolSearch can be registered optimistically but filtered from provider tools when definitive useToolSearch is false.
Deferred tools are hidden only when definitive useToolSearch is true for the request.
Haiku/unsupported model fixtures do not receive ToolSearch or tool_reference-capable results.
Default first-party proxy base URL behavior matches TS unless ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH is explicitly set.
No-deferred/no-pending requests filter ToolSearch out as TS does.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Split optimistic registration from definitive per-request use, mirroring TS. The loop should decide whether ToolSearch is active for each provider request based on env mode, beta kill switch, model support, provider/proxy support, ToolSearch availability after filtering, auto-threshold sizing, and whether there are deferred tools or pending MCP servers.

implementation_subtasks.title: Add provider-specific defer_loading, beta, and tool_reference normalization
acceptance_criteria: Go tool definitions can carry defer_loading when useToolSearch and willDefer are true, or an explicit parity decision records why client-side hiding replaces it without changing provider behavior.
Anthropic/Foundry use advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20; Vertex/Bedrock use tool-search-tool-2025-10-19 where applicable.
Tool reference blocks are stripped before provider calls when request-time ToolSearch is disabled.
References to tools no longer registered/available are stripped with a placeholder if all content is removed.
ToolReferenceBlock is never smooshed into mixed tool_result content in a provider-invalid shape.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Represent TS defer_loading in Go tool definitions or prove the provider surface no longer requires it, choose beta headers by provider exactly as TS, and normalize historical tool_reference content before provider conversion when ToolSearch is disabled or references unavailable tools.

implementation_subtasks.title: Add normal-turn deferred-tools announcements
acceptance_criteria: First active ToolSearch turn announces all currently deferred tool names in a TS-equivalent system reminder.
Subsequent turns announce only added/removed deferred tool deltas.
Announcements are suppressed when ToolSearch is not active for the request.
A fallback `<available-deferred-tools>`-style message is available if the delta path is intentionally disabled.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Implement the TS normal-turn `deferred_tools_delta` system-reminder flow, including added/removed deferred tools and the same enablement gates. Keep the existing post-compact reminder as recovery state, not as the only announcement path.

implementation_subtasks.title: Preserve loaded deferred tools through compaction and resume
acceptance_criteria: compact.discoveredToolNames finds ToolReferenceBlock values nested inside ToolResultBlock.ContentBlocks.
PreCompactDiscoveredTools contains tools loaded by ToolSearch before full, partial, snip, and session-memory compaction.
New/resumed QueryLoop rebuilds loadedToolNames from current messages and latest compact boundary metadata before building visible definitions.
A post-compact/resume integration test proves a previously loaded deferred tool remains visible without rerunning ToolSearch.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Teach Go to extract discovered tools from nested ToolResultBlock.ContentBlocks, store them in compact boundary metadata, and reconstruct QueryLoop.loadedToolNames from existing messages and compact boundary metadata on new/resumed loops.

implementation_subtasks.title: Wire MCP pending-state and dynamic invalidation into ToolSearch
acceptance_criteria: Empty select/keyword misses include pending_mcp_servers when service MCP has pending clients, matching TS output field semantics.
Failed/needs-auth/disabled richer state is either mapped behind TS-compatible pending_mcp_servers output or kept out of provider-visible ToolSearch output.
SetupRegistry wires RegisterMCPListChangedInvalidators for the ToolSearch instance it registers.
A dynamic MCP tools/list_changed integration test proves a stale cached search result is invalidated without manual test-only wiring.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Connect ToolSearch's pending/state resolvers to the actual MCP managers used by SetupRegistry, and register list_changed invalidators for the production ToolSearch instance so registry/index state refreshes when dynamic MCP tool lists change.

implementation_subtasks.title: Replace misleading ToolSearch parity tests with TS-derived goldens
acceptance_criteria: Schema tests assert `max_results` and default 5 from TS.
Search tests cover exact bare names, already-loaded exact names, MCP prefix fast path, select multi-select, required terms, searchHint scoring, and no-match pending_mcp_servers.
Provider tests cover beta stripping/selection and stale/unsupported tool_reference normalization.
Compaction/resume tests cover nested tool_reference extraction and loaded-tool reconstruction.
Any retained BM25/embedding tests are clearly labeled as Go extensions and do not block TS parity.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Rewrite the ToolSearch alignment test suite so it reflects the actual TS files in ../src. Remove or rename tests that intentionally assert Go-only experiments (limit, BM25, score/snippet metadata, embedding rerank) so they do not masquerade as parity coverage.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align ToolSearch observability and metadata
acceptance_criteria: ToolSearch outcome events include query, queryType, matchCount, totalDeferredTools, maxResults, and hasMatches.
Outcome event emission is wired to the runtime analytics/logging sink used by other tools, not only unit tests.
ToolSearch has a Go read-only marker or equivalent permission classification consumed by the loop.
ToolSearch results carry a maxResultSizeChars threshold equivalent to TS 100000 where Go's result store consumes it.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Bring Go operational metadata in line with TS: outcome analytics fields, runtime emitter wiring, read-only classification if the Go permission system supports it, and ToolSearch-specific result-size threshold metadata.

risks: Some subtasks touch shared runtime surfaces; coordinate with foundation tasks to avoid incompatible local adapters.
non_goals: Do not make unrelated behavior changes outside this tool unless required by a listed dependency.
notes_for_assignee: Start by adding or updating parity fixtures, then implement the smallest vertical slice that makes a failing fixture pass. Keep TS evidence lines in comments or test names where useful.
